source_metadata.title: Agricultural fertilization with poultry manure results in persistent environmental contamination with the pathogen Clostridioides difficile
source_metadata.authors: Martinique Frentrup; Nadine Thiel; Vera Junker; Wiebke Behrens; Steffen Münch; Paul Siller; Tina Kabelitz; Matthias Faust; Alexander Indra; Stefanie Baumgartner; Kerstin Schepanski; Thomas Amon; Uwe Roesler; Roger Funk; Ulrich Nübel
source_metadata.source_file: Environmental Microbiology - 2021 - Frentrup - Agricultural fertilization with poultry manure results in persistent.pdf

extraction_limitations: Only the main article PDF was supplied; Supplementary Fig. S1 and Supplementary Tables S1/S2 were not available for direct extraction or validation.
Environmental C. difficile in soil and dust was enrichment-culture positive but not quantifiable by direct plating, so concentration trajectories and a decay rate cannot be extracted.
The article reports genomic relatedness to external human and chicken-meat isolates but does not provide epidemiological linkage proving direct zoonotic transmission.
The PDF does not contain a distinct conflict-of-interest statement; no conflict_of_interest atom was created.
